title: ES 4 RXV · One-candle pullback continuation
summary: Earlier trend → one opposite candle → resumption. Compare saved results by earlier trend length, direction, year and all seven session windows; exact counts are downloadable.

sections.title: Read the A → B → R setup
sections.body: A is a consecutive original-direction leg, B is exactly one completed opposite-colour candle, and R is the next completed candle returning to A's direction. All three are adjacent within the same eligible session. Bullish example: bullish A1,A2,A3 → bearish B → bullish R → bullish F1 → bullish F2. This has earlier A length 3 and succeeds at n=2; R and B are excluded from n. Bearish events mirror that sequence. The earlier trend filter measures A, not the one-candle B pullback. A must have an observed completed end at B. Exact known starts use the whole A length; unknown A starts have their own group. An A length of one can be simple alternating candles and is not treated as a substantial trend. Choose year, session and earlier trend length in the tables. All years + All hours gives overall; a year + All hours gives yearly; All years + a named window gives session; a year + a window gives year-by-session. The All earlier legs row overlaps the disjoint size rows; do not sum it with them. Continuation requires n uninterrupted completed candles with R's close-open sign. An opposite candle or doji is failure. A session/export boundary before classification is unknown. Already-observed short-horizon successes remain counted. Rates use each horizon's known success + failure population; exact numerator, denominator and unknown counts for every cell are in the four CSVs.

sections.title: Timing, windows and interpretation
sections.body: Event groups use R's completion proxy (when the signal becomes known), rather than its opening or outcome time. Year uses its inferred 18:00-rollover session date. Follow-up continues across named-window endpoints but never across inferred daily sessions or completion barriers. NY wall-time windows: Asia 20:00–02:00; London 02:00–09:00; NY 09:30–16:00; Asia Open 19:30–21:30; NY Open 09:30–10:30; NY AM 10:30–12:30; NY PM 12:30–16:00. Start included, end excluded. Overlapping windows cannot all be summed. 2019 and 2026 have partial coverage. The entire partial final session 2026-09-24 is excluded. Bar coverage is anchored at bar opening, separately from event completion-time groups. Original same-second and identical rows retain source order. OHLC is available; volume, exact completion and contract/roll treatment are unverified. These are descriptive historical frequencies on already-inspected history, without independent forecast validation, iid confidence intervals or trading profitability evidence.

notes: Pooled-direction results and exact unrounded counts/rates for every year, window and earlier-leg cohort are included in CSVs. Displayed rates retain six decimals before formatting.
Continuation uses candle colour; F1 recovery uses its close relative to R.close. A gap can make these outcomes differ.

downloads.label: Probabilities · all earlier legs and horizons
downloads.description: Exact saved strings, including all 15 earlier-leg cohorts, all directions, overall, yearly, seven windows and year-by-window. Blank estimates are undefined. All cohort overlaps its size cohorts; do not sum them together.
downloads.population: Observed completed A → single opposite B → same-direction R setups. Unknown future outcomes are separately retained; earlier unknown-start legs have their own cohort.
downloads.units: Probabilities are ratios; counts are setups or sessions as labeled. n is additional candles after R; depth is percent of R body.
downloads.scope: ES 4 RXV · continuation · 2019–2026 observed history; final partial session excluded.
